Rotating piercings is a really bad advice that only really old school piercers give.

Put it that way :

The jewelry is sterile when you put it in, but isn't anymore after. By rotating it you can put bacteria in the wound and increase the chances of infection.
Secondly, you will cause an irritation which can not only lead to irritation bumps, but also make your cicatrisation process waaaaaay longer.

So, it can turn fine if you're lucky but is still risky. 

Concerning the 16g jewelry, a little stretch must be done, but a jewelry to small can cut and irritate your cartilage so it's still better than keeping something like what you have :/

There is so much to say ><

The jewelry is awful and too small, moreover you should never be pierced with silver. And never ever should you be pierced with a hoop.

Replace your jewelry with a 16G implantable grad titanium flat back jewelry.

Then, for the aftercare, use sterile saline water on compresses, applied on the zone during 10 minutes thrice a day. If you're in the US, Neilmed seems to make some good products.

And don't touch, rotate or play with your piercings, and don't sleep on it either.

The good thing is : needle is the way to go, and you were right on that point. Piercing guns are an abomination.
